audit_findings.title: The zero-growth bear case omits credible negative CRM-transition downside
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer losses, migration costs, pricing concessions, and added Vault infrastructure expense could reduce future OE and make growth negative through 2030.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, Salesforce, our primary CRM competitor, has announced that certain large Veeva CRM customers have committed to purchasing its CRM solutions and a number of our customers have informed us of their intent to move to Salesforce as their CRM provider.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed customer decisions demonstrate that attrition risk is real, but the filings do not quantify the CRM revenue, margin, or migration costs at risk. The financial effect remains forward-looking and is not established in the current OE anchor. It could materially lower the bear value, although it would reinforce rather than reverse the present conclusion because even the $115.64 bull value is far below the $275.09 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain CRM recurring revenue and margin by departing customer, contracted migration schedules, concessions, and incremental Vault CRM costs; rerun a contraction scenario through 2030.

audit_findings.title: The valuation mixes a pre-acquisition earnings anchor with a post-acquisition balance sheet and share count
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $90 million consideration, $70 million net of cash acquired, and $81.833 million acquisition cash outflow; acquired OE and retention-award dilution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The July cash bridge reflects the acquisition payment, while the FY2026 OE anchor excludes Ostro's post-acquisition profits or losses; unmodeled retention awards could also affect fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Veeva completed the acquisition of Ostro for approximately $ 100 million in cash and long-term equity retention grants.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. The post-acquisition $7,242.947 million cash-and-STI bridge already reflects the transaction, so another purchase-price deduction would double count it. Missing Ostro earnings could raise or lower OE, and the filing does not quantify the separately accounted-for retention awards. The $90 million consideration is only 0.46% of the $19.473 billion base equity value, but the record cannot establish the scale of recurring losses, profits, or dilution.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile Ostro's post-close revenue, operating cash costs, maintenance investment, assumed liabilities, cash acquired, and retention-award share equivalents, then rerun on a consistently post-acquisition perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized internal software may escape the maintenance-capital charge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed FY2026 total long-term-assets outflow of $29.131 million; internal-software portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any omitted internal-use software additions would reduce the $698.4 million OE anchor as maintenance investment.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalize certain costs incurred for the development of computer software for internal use.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the calculation captured these additions is unresolved, but the entire FY2026 long-term-assets outflow limits the possible anchor omission to $29.131 million. Treating all of it as omitted would reduce the anchor by 4.2%, the base operating value by about $510 million, and base value by about $2.83 per share, from $107.82 to roughly $104.99. That cannot change the conclusion relative to the $275.09 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2026 $29.131 million long-term-assets outflow to internal-use software and other capital additions and confirm the exact amount already deducted in maintenance investment.

audit_findings.title: A genuine litigation one-off appears retained in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $30.627 million pre-tax; computed approximately $23.3 million after tax using the filed 23.9% effective tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining the non-recurring charge reduces normalized OE and therefore operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: We paid approximately $ 31 million to certain law firms with whom we entered into partial contingency fee arrangements, pursuant to which such law firms were entitled to a success fee if certain non-monetary outcomes are achieved.
audit_findings.explanation: The payment and dismissal with prejudice demonstrate a genuine one-off, so retaining it is conservative rather than value inflation. Adding back approximately $23.3 million after tax would increase the anchor by 3.3%, base operating value by about $408 million, and base value by about $2.26 per share to roughly $110.08. This remains far below the $275.09 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm explicitly whether the charge was intentionally retained; if normalization is desired, add back only its verified after-tax amount and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Potential tax claims were not visibly reconciled in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $41.547 million gross unrecognized tax benefits plus approximately $4 million accrued interest and penalties at January 31, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: A payable tax amount not already captured through tax expense or normalized OE would be deducted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 31, 2026, the total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits was $ 42 million, of which $ 26 million, if recognized, would favorably impact our effective tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The absence of a visible reconciliation is demonstrated, but an incremental equity claim is not: uncertain-tax liabilities are already recognized within reported liabilities and related tax effects may already enter OE. Even deducting the entire approximately $45.5 million identified amount would reduce the $19.473 billion base equity value by only 0.23%, or about $0.25 per share. The July filing also reports only $33.708 million of total other long-term liabilities, indicating that the January amount is not an appropriate automatic additional deduction.
audit_findings.action: Map the July uncertain-tax balance, accrued interest and penalties, current tax payable, and settlements to reported liabilities and OE; deduct only a verified amount not already economically captured.

audit_findings.title: Public-benefit status weakens the assumption that all owner earnings serve common shareholders exclusively
audit_findings.mechanism: Board-approved allocations benefiting non-stockholder constituencies could reduce cash distributable to common shareholders or affect sale-of-control proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: Further, as a PBC, our Board is required to balance our stockholders’ pecuniary (financial) interests, the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and pursuit of our public benefit purpose.
audit_findings.explanation: The PBC balancing obligation is demonstrated, but it is not a fixed claim and the supplied record identifies no measurable historical diversion of OE. Any valuation effect depends on future board decisions, so it is not presently in the numbers and cannot be quantified.
audit_findings.action: Review historical capital allocation, annual public-benefit reports, stakeholder spending, and any transactions where the board accepted a measurable financial tradeoff; model a deduction only if a persistent amount is established.
